hint.en: Grid voltage used for watt/amp conversions everywhere - with Household phases below for the household cap, and with the EV charger's own Phases setting for solar and charger-circuit calculations. Use the nominal value for your grid (e.g. 230) - it doesn't need to track the live measured voltage.

Your home's main fuse/breaker rating per phase, matching Household phases below - most main breakers are amp-rated, not watt-rated. Charging is throttled in any mode so total grid import never exceeds this. Set 0 to disable.

How many phases your home's main supply has (independent of the EV charger's own Phases setting below - a single-phase charger on a 3-phase household connection is common). Used with Main fuse rating and Nominal voltage above to compute the household grid cap.

How many phases the charger is wired on (1 or 3). Used with Nominal voltage (under Household electrical above) for solar and charger-circuit watt/amp conversions, and sent to the charger in every charging profile.

Lowest current ever sent to the charger once it's told to charge - manual, scheduled, and solar targets are all floored to this. Also the surplus threshold: solar charging only starts once available surplus reaches at least this many amps.
Highest current ever sent to the charger, in any mode. Manual, scheduled, and solar targets are all capped to this - match it to what the charger and your home's wiring/breaker support.

Set this if the charger's own circuit/breaker has a lower rating than the rest of the house - whether it's dedicated to the charger alone (e.g. a 32A breaker with nothing else on it) or shared with other equipment (e.g. a home battery inverter, or any other load). Charging is throttled in any mode so total current on that circuit never exceeds this. This is independent of the whole-household grid cap under Household electrical. Set 0 to disable.

Enable if solar PV also feeds into the charger circuit above - its production is added as extra headroom on top of the circuit rating. Leave off if the circuit has nothing to do with your solar system (or you have none).

Enable if a home battery inverter also feeds into the charger circuit above - its charge/discharge is netted into the circuit rating, and battery discharge blocks a schedule's boost-to-cap from treating it as spare capacity. Leave off if the circuit has nothing to do with a battery (or you have none).
Amps reserved on the charger circuit for anything not otherwise measured (e.g. inverter overhead, other appliances). Subtracted from the circuit rating before any of it is offered to the EV.

Authorization tag sent when the app starts a charging session itself (manual/schedule/solar). By default any idTag is accepted, so this only needs to match something if you've enabled an idTag whitelist in the app's own settings.

How often the charger itself is configured to report power/current/voltage/energy (OCPP MeterValues), in seconds. Lower values give more responsive solar tracking and a livelier dashboard, at the cost of more OCPP traffic.

Minimum spacing between charging-profile (current limit) writes sent to the charger. Prevents a fast-moving solar target from flooding the charger with SetChargingProfile calls; it also delays how quickly a new target actually reaches the charger.

When off, the charger never derives Solar mode outside a schedule - it goes Idle (holds at 0A) instead. Manual and Scheduled modes are unaffected, and the surplus meter/household caps keep updating in the background so re-enabling takes effect immediately.
Watts held back before offering surplus to the EV. Positive reserves headroom and charges more conservatively; negative allows a bit of grid import. 0 targets breakeven.
While already charging, ignore surplus changes smaller than this many amps. Stops the current limit from adjusting on every minor solar flicker.
While already charging, the most the current limit can change by on any single solar update. Smooths out sudden swings instead of jumping straight to the new target.
Once solar charging starts, keep it running at least this long before a temporary drop in surplus is allowed to pause it.
Once paused (or before a first start), surplus must stay sufficient for at least this long before charging (re)starts. Prevents rapid pause/resume cycling.
If no solar reading arrives for this long, solar charging pauses as a fail-safe until fresh data returns.
Your system's peak PV output, used only to show a % capacity meter on the dashboard widget's Solar tile. Set 0 to hide that meter.
Your battery's peak charge power, used only to show a % capacity meter on the dashboard widget's Battery tile while charging. Set 0 to hide that meter.
Your battery's peak discharge power, used only to show a % capacity meter on the dashboard widget's Battery tile while discharging. Set 0 to hide that meter.
